newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl wants EMU in 1999, but no easing of criteria.
newsitem.headline: Kohl wants EMU in 1999, but no easing of criteria.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said in an article published on Tuesday that Europe's single currency should be launched on time in 1999, but he would not accept a softening of the Maastricht criteria to meet that timetable.
"We want the euro to come punctually on January 1, 1999," Kohl wrote in the Deutsche Sparkassenzeitung. "But it is clear that this must not be at the expense of monetary stability."
Kohl added: "The stability criteria of the Maastricht treaty are not open to discussion."
In a separate interview with the Die Zeit weekly, Kohl's heir-apparent Wolfgang Schaeuble said that fulfilling the convergence criteria was "an absolute priority" for Germany.
Schaeuble, who is parliamentary leader of Kohl's Christian Democrats (CDU), also said he strongly opposed a delay to European monetary union (EMU).

"We must fulfil the criteria, so that we do not have to postpone the euro. It is doubtful whether Europe would get a second chance after a delay," Schaeuble said in an interview released ahead of publication on Thursday.
